# AGENT-11

> AGENT-11 is a free, open-source multi-agent development framework for Claude Code, built by Jamie Watters. One install command deploys 11 specialist agents into a project's `.claude/` directory, and work is then run as structured missions through the `/coord` command. agent-11.com is the framework's marketing and documentation site; the source code and the full manuals live in the GitHub repository.

Last updated: 2026-07-26. Current framework release: v6.2.0, "Loop Discipline & Read-Only Verification", published 2026-06-20.

Install, into any project directory:

`bash <(curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/TheWayWithin/agent-11/main/project/deployment/scripts/secure-install.sh)`

The 11 specialists, all deployed by every install: coordinator, strategist, architect, developer, designer, tester, documenter, operator, analyst, marketer, support.

The 13 missions routed through `/coord`: build, mvp, dev-setup, dev-alignment, integrate, migrate, fix, refactor, optimize, document, release, deploy, security.

AGENT-11 is free and MIT licensed. There is no paid tier, subscription, or per-mission charge; the only cost of running it is your own Claude Code / Anthropic usage. The agents run locally inside your project — there is no AGENT-11 server and no account to create.

## Start here

- [AGENT-11 home](https://agent-11.com/): What the framework is, the install command, the 11 specialists, worked examples of `/coord` usage, and how AGENT-11 was used to build itself.
- [Documentation](https://agent-11.com/documentation): The site's single-page manual — quick start, the 13 missions with their `/coord` usage strings and typical durations, agent roles, configuration, the context-preservation protocol (`agent-context.md`, `project-plan.md`, `evidence-repository.md`), MCP integration, and troubleshooting.
- [Features](https://agent-11.com/features): All 13 missions as filterable cards by category and complexity, the v6.2 quality-gate and loop-discipline features, the slash commands, the 11 agents by squad tier, and the seven SaaS skills (auth, payments, multitenancy, billing, email, onboarding, analytics).

## Source and manuals

- [agent-11 on GitHub](https://github.com/TheWayWithin/agent-11): The framework itself. MIT licensed, default branch `main`.
- [README](https://github.com/TheWayWithin/agent-11/blob/main/README.md): The fullest single description of the framework: squad composition, mission library, commands, and configuration.
- [QUICK-START.md](https://github.com/TheWayWithin/agent-11/blob/main/QUICK-START.md): Getting from install to a first mission. Note that its install snippets are older than the canonical `secure-install.sh` command in the README.
- [INSTALLATION.md](https://github.com/TheWayWithin/agent-11/blob/main/INSTALLATION.md): Install paths, requirements, and what the installer writes to `.claude/`.
- [TROUBLESHOOTING.md](https://github.com/TheWayWithin/agent-11/blob/main/TROUBLESHOOTING.md): Common install and mission failures and their fixes.
- [Field manual](https://github.com/TheWayWithin/agent-11/tree/main/project/field-manual): The long-form guides — coordinator protocol, mission execution, quality gates, loop discipline, memory management, MCP integration, model selection, plan-driven development.
- [Mission library](https://github.com/TheWayWithin/agent-11/blob/main/project/missions/library.md): The mission catalogue, with the individual mission definitions alongside it in the same directory.
- [Agent profiles](https://github.com/TheWayWithin/agent-11/tree/main/project/agents): The specialist definitions themselves — one file per agent, plus the core-squad and full-squad rosters.
- [CHANGELOG.md](https://github.com/TheWayWithin/agent-11/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md): Release-by-release history maintained in the repository.
- [Releases](https://github.com/TheWayWithin/agent-11/releases): Tagged releases; the most recent is `v6.2.0-loop-discipline`.
- [Issues](https://github.com/TheWayWithin/agent-11/issues): Bug reports and feature requests. This is the framework's support channel.
- [LICENSE](https://github.com/TheWayWithin/agent-11/blob/main/LICENSE): The MIT licence text as it ships with the framework.

## About the project

- [Changelog](https://agent-11.com/changelog): The framework's release history, newest first, from v1.0.0 (2023-12-01) to v6.2.0 (2026-06-20), with per-release added/fixed/changed notes. Every version listed is mirrored from the repository CHANGELOG, which remains authoritative. Note there is no 3.x line, and two repository tags have no CHANGELOG entry so are not listed.
- [Pricing](https://agent-11.com/pricing): Confirms the free, MIT-licensed, single-tier model, lists what an install includes, and gives the voluntary ways to support the author. Nothing is sold on this site.
- [Support](https://agent-11.com/support): How to get help — the documentation and GitHub Issues — plus FAQs on installing, cost, and where your code goes.
- [About Jamie Watters](https://agent-11.com/about): Why the framework was built, the author's background and stated principles, and links to his other projects.

## Optional

- [License](https://agent-11.com/license): The MIT licence reproduced on-site with a plain-English reading. The repository `LICENSE` file is the authoritative text.
- [Portfolio](https://agent-11.com/portfolio): Jamie Watters' wider set of tools. Mostly about products other than AGENT-11, and several entries are at planning or in-development stage.
- [Privacy policy](https://agent-11.com/privacy): Site privacy policy, rewritten 2026-07-25 to match what the site actually does. No cookies are set and no tracking is used; visits are counted with cookieless Plausible analytics, and the only personal data the site can hold is an email address voluntarily submitted through its Netlify-hosted form.
- [Terms of service](https://agent-11.com/terms): Site terms, rewritten 2026-07-25. States plainly that there is no payment, no subscription and no account, and that the software is governed by the MIT licence. Consistent with /pricing and the repository LICENSE.
- [Sitemap](https://agent-11.com/sitemap.xml): Machine-readable index of every page on this site.
